title: Salesforce Agentforce Flaw Lets Attackers Steal CRM Data With Zero-Click Prompt Injection
content_md: A newly disclosed, now-remediated Salesforce Agentforce vulnerability chain, dubbed SalesBleed, could have enabled attackers to extract sensitive CRM data through a zero-click indirect prompt injection attack . The attack began with a malicious submission to a public Salesforce Web-to-Lead form and required neither Salesforce credentials nor a victim click. Zenity Labs reported that Salesforce investigated the findings after responsible disclosure and addressed the specific Trusted URLs bypasses used in the research. Salesforce Agentforce Flaw The vulnerabilities were reported on June 1, 2026, and Zenity later confirmed the fixes; Salesforce also said it found no evidence of exploitation in the wild. URL redaction layer was bypassed (Source: Zenity Labs) Salesforce Web-to-Lead forms are intentionally exposed to unauthenticated users, so prospective customers can submit contact details. According to Zenity , an attacker could place hidden instructions inside a lead field, creating a poisoned CRM record that remained dormant until an employee later asked Agentforce to review recent leads. A routine request, such as asking the agent to check the newest lead, could cause Agentforce to process attacker-controlled content. The injected instructions could then manipulate the General CRM subagent into invoking its existing Query Records capability against other accessible Salesforce objects, including Account records.
